title: Amazon-Uber Eats Deal Sends DASH Stock To Biggest Drop In A Year
detail:

Anan Ashraf

DASH
UBER
CART
Explore stocks on Coinbase

Amazon estimates frequent users could save more than $175 a year, a figure that exceeds the cost of an annual Prime membership.

The partnership hands Uber Eats immediate reach into Amazon's large, high-engagement Prime base, raising competition for DoorDash.

DoorDash agreed to acquire Instacart (CART) in a deal valued at roughly $17 billion, or $65 per share last month.

Shares of DoorDash (DASH) slumped 10% on Thursday after rivals Amazon (AMZN) and Uber Technologies (UBER) struck a partnership giving Amazon Prime members free delivery on Uber Eats restaurant orders of $25 or more when placed directly through Amazon's website or app.

Under the arrangement, which took effect immediately, Prime subscribers can browse and order from hundreds of thousands of restaurants without creating a separate Uber account or leaving the Amazon platform. Amazon handles payment and delivery notifications, while Uber Eats fulfills the orders. The $0 delivery fee applies U.S.-wide, across nearly 10,000 cities and towns.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

The deal replaces Amazon's previous partnership with Grubhub, which ended the same day. Amazon estimates frequent users could save more than $175 a year, a figure that exceeds the cost of an annual Prime membership, though service fees still apply.

The partnership hands Uber Eats immediate reach into Amazon's large, high-engagement Prime base, raising competition for DoorDash which commands a dominant share of U.S. restaurant delivery spending. DASH stock is no on track for its worst day in a year, if the losses hold.

The sell-off on Thursday comes less than two weeks after DoorDash agreed to acquire Instacart (CART) in a deal valued at roughly $17 billion, or $65 per share. The combination is intended to strengthen DoorDash's position in grocery and expand its local commerce platform. The transaction, expected to close in late 2027 or early 2028, remains subject to regulatory review.

How Did DASH Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around DASH stock fell from 'bullish' to 'neutral' territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume skidded from 'high' to 'normal' levels.

DASH stock has dropped 22% year-to-date.

title: dYdX Team’s Arcus Opens Stock-Token Collateral to All Perps Traders, With a $20,000 Cap
detail:
dYdX Team’s Arcus Opens Stock-Token Collateral to All Perps Traders, With a $20,000 Cap
Arcus opens stock-token collateral to all perps traders
Unchained

ETHDYDX-USD
WETH-USD
USDG33793-USD
QQQ
AAPL
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Arcus, the Robinhood Chain exchange developed by the team that built dYdX, has opened Multi-Asset Collateral to every trader with access to its perpetual futures, removing the trading-volume requirement that had limited the feature since October. The company announced the change on Thursday.

As in early access, Arcus caps deposits of assets other than USDG at $20,000 per user and $2 million across the platform. Each account can borrow at most $10,000, according to Arcus's public lending data, and the exchange rejects orders that would push a loan past that limit. By Unchained's math, 100 traders depositing the $20,000 maximum would fill the platform-wide cap.

Traders can now back perps positions with ether, held as wrapped ether (WETH), and nine stock tokens alongside USDG, which most Arcus traders had needed for perps margin until now. The stock tokens are SPY, QQQ, Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia, Meta and Tesla, the last seven of which the press release groups as "MAG7." Each asset carries a 50% initial loan-to-value ratio.

Get Unchained's crypto news in your inbox with the free Unchained Daily newsletter.

Early Access Began Oct. 19

Arcus started rolling out the feature on Oct. 19 to accounts with more than $25 million in trading volume on the exchange, with the same assets and the same 50% ratio. Other traders do not need to switch anything on, according to Thursday's post.

How the Loans Work

The borrowing is automatic: once tokens sit in the perps account, any margin or losses the trader's USDG doesn't cover become a variable-rate loan that shrinks as the margin need falls. That rate was 4.94% a year on Thursday, according to Arcus's public lending feed. If falling token prices or a growing loan push the account past a maintenance level set for each asset, or the loan exceeds the per-account cap, Arcus can liquidate it, closing perps positions, selling the tokens, or both.

"Spot positions and perpetuals positions shouldn't have to operate in separate silos," founder and CEO Eddie Zhang said in the press release. He said the feature lets traders put stock token value to work "whether they're looking to maintain an existing position, put on a new trade or hedge their exposure."

Arcus, in which Robinhood Crypto is a strategic investor, is not available in the U.S., Canada or the U.K. The exchange launched leveraged stock and crypto tokens in August, and Robinhood Wallet began routing stock token trades through it on Oct. 1.

title: Amazon Stocks Decline 3.52% With AWS Profitability in Focus
detail:
Amazon Stocks Decline 3.52% With AWS Profitability in Focus

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) traded at $256.68, down 3.52%, at 10:45 a.m. ET in November 5 regular trading. The retail and cloud giant's session data showed shares under pressure, while its October 29 earnings put one business firmly in focus: AWS. Cloud demand and the cost of expanding AI infrastructure remain central to the investment case.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with AMZN.

AMZN GF Value chart

Amazon's third-quarter results showed revenue of $201.9 billion and operating income of $28.1 billion. AWS contributed $46 billion in revenue and $17.8 billion in operating income, with cloud sales climbing 39.3% year over year against 12% growth across the company. That means AWS produced roughly 63% of operating income from just 23% of revenue, with an operating margin near 39%. These are the previously reported quarterly figures, rather than a fresh update on November 5.

The GuruFocus snapshot adds another angle: a GF Score of 94/100, with growth the strongest chart component and financial strength comparatively weaker. It also flags two severe warning signs without identifying them, so the high score deserves context. For investors, the spending question cuts both ways. Slower expansion could preserve cash in the near term, while too little capacity could hold back cloud revenue. AWS growth, capacity utilization and cash generation could help show whether Amazon's infrastructure spending is paying off.
